reason: The cited evidence only confirms that HfNbTaTiZr is a refractory alloy with useful strength and that 'anti-oxidation coatings are still required' for such alloys, but it provides no specific data on alumina-forming coatings, their effectiveness on this alloy, or their impact on mechanical properties. The key premises about coating performance and property retention are entirely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxidation resistance at high temperature
Alumina-forming coatings can provide oxidation protection for refractory alloys
A thin coating can form a protective Al2O3 scale that acts as a diffusion barrier
The coating will not degrade the alloy's room-temperature ductility or high-temperature strength
The protective effect will persist for ~100 hours at 1000 °C under mechanical loading
